note: FILLING IS NOT WRAPPING: it re-flows what is there. Emacs answers ("aa bb cc" "aa bb cc"). The first element shows existing newlines INSIDE a paragraph being joined away when the text now fits -- `s-word-wrap' on a string that already has newlines in it is therefore not a no-op -- and the second shows runs of spaces squeezed to one and trailing whitespace dropped, which is NOSQUEEZE nil, the default s.el gets. Both are properties a from-scratch wrapper that only ever inserts newlines would fail. kg answers `void-function' at this pin.
